title: The ALMA Survey of 70 µm Dark High-mass Clumps in Early Stages (ASHES). XIII. Core Mass Function, Lifetime, and Growth of Prestellar Cores
question: What are the universality, power-law slope, lifetime, and mass growth properties of the prestellar core mass function (CMF) in the earliest stages of high-mass star formation within 70 μm dark IRDC clumps?

data.arrays: 12-m array, 7-m array, Total Power (TP; for spectral line data only)

what.value: NH3 rotational temperatures at ~5'' for cores in eleven ASHES clumps

evidence.quote: For cores in eleven ASHES clumps, we used the rotational temperatures derived from NH$_3$ observations at $\sim$5$''$ (cite: Li23; Allingham24).
For the remaining twenty-eight clumps, we adopted the clump temperature for the core mass calculation (cite: Guzman15).

what.value: Core catalog (839 cores), continuum properties, and temperatures used for mass estimation (Table 4)

evidence.quote: Column 3 in Table 4 in (cite: Morii23) shows the temperature used for each core in the mass estimation.
By applying the dendrogram technique, implemented in `astrodendro` (cite: Rosolowsky08), to the 1.3 mm continuum images of 39 regions, we have identified 839 cores (cite: Morii23).

what.value: Core evolutionary classifications and virial parameters

evidence.quote: Detailed information and line setups are described in (cite: Morii24).

Among 839 cores, either of the lines is detected from 492 cores (58.6%), and 340 cores (69.1%) have virial parameter smaller than 2, classified as gravitationally bound cores ignoring external pressure and the magnetic field (cite: Morii24).

what.value: Dust opacity at 1.3 mm of 0.9 cm^2 g^-1

evidence.quote: We adopt the standard gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100, and a dust opacity of 0.9 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: Ossenkopf94).

what.value: CMF power-law indices from the ALMA-IMF project for comparison

evidence.quote: For comparison, we plotted the index and the uncertainties estimated in some studies of the ALMA-IMF project (cite: Nony23; Pouteau23; Louvet24).

recipe.goal: Identify cores, classify evolutionary stages, and assess gravitational binding
recipe.method: Extract cores from 1.3 mm continuum images of 39 regions using astrodendro (and getsf with 10 arcsec maximum size for comparison); classify into outflow cores, warm cores, and prestellar core candidates using CO (2-1) and warm gas tracers (H2CO, CH3OH, HC3N); compute virial parameters from DCO+ and N2D+ (3-2) velocity dispersions.
key_parameters: virial parameter < 2 for gravitationally bound cores; getsf maximum source size = 10 arcsec
assumptions: Ignore external pressure and magnetic field in virial analysis

recipe.goal: Calculate core masses and verify optically thin dust emission
recipe.method: Compute core masses from 1.3 mm continuum flux density using Equation 1, and check optical depth at 1.3 mm using the ratio of peak intensity over beam solid angle to the Planck function.
key_parameters: gas-to-dust mass ratio R = 100; dust opacity kappa_nu = 0.9 cm^2 g^-1
assumptions: Optically thin 1.3 mm dust continuum emission; NH3 rotational temperatures for 11 clumps and clump temperatures for 28 clumps

recipe.goal: Evaluate mass completeness, apply flux recovery correction, and select final core sample
recipe.method: Insert artificial Gaussian cores into continuum images at uniformly random positions where primary beam response > 40%, run astrodendro 5000 times to measure detection rate and flux recovery per mass bin, exclude 5 clumps with lowest completeness, and divide observed core masses by the recovery fraction where completeness > 0.5.
key_parameters: 5000 trials; primary beam response > 40%; 90% completeness threshold = 1.2 M_sun after excluding 5 clumps; flux correction applied where completeness > 0.5

recipe.goal: Construct CMFs and fit power-law slopes
recipe.method: Construct differential histograms (using numpy Freedman Diaconis Estimator for bin edges), variable-bin complementary cumulative distributions, and unbinned distributions; fit power-law indices above 1.2 M_sun and evaluate 1sigma uncertainties via 1000-trial Monte Carlo simulations of 50% mass uncertainties.
key_parameters: M_min = 1.2 M_sun; 1000 Monte Carlo trials with mass scaling factor uniformly in 0.5-1.5

recipe.goal: Estimate statistical lifetime of prestellar cores as a function of mass
recipe.method: Compute statistical lifetime of gravitationally bound prestellar cores relative to bound protostellar cores overall and in logarithmic mass bins using Equation 2.
key_parameters: reference protostellar lifetime t_proto = 0.2 Myr; freefall time t_ff ~ 3 x 10^4 yr
assumptions: Constant star formation rate throughout the cloud's lifetime; baseline constant core mass over time, plus alternative scenarios with M_proto = 2 * M_obs (accretion onto protostar) and M_proto = 0.5 * M_obs (core growth)

recipe.goal: Model core mass growth and infer external mass infall rate from CMF evolution
recipe.method: Compare observed bound prestellar and protostellar CMFs with Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton (BHL) accretion and fit a power-law external mass infall model (M_dot = C * M^p) using scipy curve_fit.
key_parameters: n_cl = 4 x 10^4 cm^-3; sigma_cl = 1 km s^-1; external infall duration = 30 kyr
assumptions: External mass infall rate follows a power-law dependence on core mass over a constant duration of 30 kyr

score_reason: The statistical, CMF fitting, completeness, lifetime, and infall modeling steps are clearly described with standard Python packages (astrodendro, powerlaw, scipy, numpy), and the core catalogs/temperatures are published in companion papers (Morii et al. 2023, 2024), though exact astrodendro thresholds and the FITS continuum maps are needed to exactly replicate the injection-recovery flux corrections.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA datasets (Cycles 3, 5, 6) and companion catalogs (Morii et al. 2023, 2024) are public, the core extraction and power-law fitting recipes are well-specified, and the main results are concrete numerical slopes, lifetimes, and infall parameters.
